chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Salim, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Qatada, all from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out for the display of the horses, and passed by the grave of Abu Uhayhah. So Abu Bakr said, 'May Allah curse the occupant of this grave, for by Allah, he used to divert people from the way of Allah and deny the Messenger of Allah.' So Khalid, his son, said, 'Rather, may Allah curse Abu Qahafa (Abu Bakr's father), for by Allah, he neither hosted guests nor fought the enemy.' So may Allah curse the more worthless of the two in the clan. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) placed the bridle of his mount on its shoulder, then said, 'When you mention the polytheists, speak in general terms and do not be specific, lest his son become angry.'

Then he stopped and the horses were presented to him. A horse passed by him, and Uyayna ibn Hisn said, 'Such and such is the matter of this horse.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Leave us, for I am more knowledgeable of horses than you.' Uyayna said, 'And I am more knowledgeable of men than you.'

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) became angry until blood appeared in his face. He said to him, 'So which of the men are the best?' Uyayna ibn Hisn said, 'Men who are in Najd, placing their swords on their shoulders and their spears on the saddles of their horses, then striking with them forward, forward.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'You are lying. Rather, the men of Yemen are best. Faith is Yemeni and wisdom is Yemeni, and if it were not for the Hijrah, I would have been a man of the people of Yemen.'

Alienation and harshness are in the Fadadeen (owners of wool), the people of the hair, Rabi'ah and Muzar from where the horn of the sun rises. And Muzhaj, most of the tribe will enter Paradise. And Hazramaut is better than Amr ibn Sa'sa' (and some narrated: better than al-Harith ibn Mu'awiya). And Bajila is better than Ra'il and Dhakwan. And if Liyan were to perish, I would not care.

Then he said, 'May Allah curse the four kings: Jamad, Makhwas, Mashrah, and Abza'a, and their sister al-Ammaradah. May Allah curse the Muhallil (one who legalizes a woman for her previous husband after three divorces) and the one to whom she is legalized, and the one who follows other than his masters, and the one who claims a lineage that is not known, and the men who imitate women, and the women who imitate men, and the one who innovates a new matter in Islam or hosts an innovator, and the one who kills someone other than the one who killed him, or strikes someone other than the one who struck him, and the one who curses his parents.'

A man said, 'O Messenger of Allah, is there a man who curses his parents?' He said, 'Yes, he curses the fathers and mothers of the men, so they curse his parents.' May Allah curse Ra'il, Dhakwan, Azl, Liyan, and the Mujdamin from Asad and Ghatafan, and Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and Shahbal the two-toothed, and the two sons of Malik ibn Jazim, and Marwan, and Hawdhah, and Hawnah.

key_terms.أَبُو أُحَيْحَةَ: Abu Uhayhah, a companion whose grave was passed by the Prophet
key_terms.أَبُو قُحَافَةَ: Abu Qahafa, the father of Abu Bakr
key_terms.الْمُحَلِّل: The Muhallil, one who legalizes a woman for her previous husband after three divorces
key_terms.رَبِيعَةَ وَ مُضَر: Rabi'ah and Muzar, major Arab tribes
key_terms.عُرْضُ الْخَيْلِ: The display or exhibition of horses

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the superiority of Yemeni people over Najd people?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Al-Kafi, illustrates the Prophet’s (saww) emphasis on avoiding specific curses to prevent broader familial repercussions, a principle derived from his reaction to Abu Bakr cursing Abu Uhayhah. It further establishes the theological superiority of the Yemeni tribes in faith and wisdom over the Najd tribes, reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition of valuing the 'Yamani' lineage. The narrative concludes with a comprehensive list of curses against specific pre-Islamic kings and tribes, highlighting the historical context of tribal rivalries and their spiritual consequences.

en.hubeali: H 14475 – Abu Ali Al-Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Saalim and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father altogether, from Ahmad Bin Al-Nazar, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Abu Al-Qasim, from Al-Husayn Bin Abu Qatada altogether, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, who said: Abu Ja’farasws

having said: ‘The Messenger<sup>as</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> came out for the display of the horses. He<sup>saww</sup> passed by the grave of Abu Ahayhat. So Abu Bakr said, ‘Curse be upon the occupant of this grave, for by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, he used to divert people away from the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and belied the Messenger<sup>saww</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’. So Khalid, his (Ahayhat’s) son said, ‘But curse of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> be upon Abu Qohafa (Abu Bakr’s father), for by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, he neither served a guest nor did he kill (fight) the enemy. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Cursed the worthless one of the two of his clan’. 
So the Messenger<sup>saww</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> placed the bridle of the horse upon his (Abu Bakr’s) neck and said: ‘Whenever you speak about the ‘Mushraqeen’ Polytheists speak in general terms and not particular, for you have anger his son’.

Then he<sup>saww</sup> paused. The horses were displayed to him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>saww</sup> passed by a horse. Uyayna Bin Hisan said, ‘The matter of this horse is such and such’. The Messenger<sup>saww</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> said: ‘Leave us, for I<sup>saww</sup> am more knowledgeable of the horses than you are’. Uyayna said, ‘And I am more knowledgeable of the men than you<sup>saww</sup> are’ (Nouzobillah).

So the Messenger<sup>saww</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> got angry to the extent that blood appeared in his<sup>saww</sup> face. He<sup>saww</sup> said to him: ‘So which of the men are the best?’ Uyayna Bin Hisan said, ‘The men who are in Najd place their swords upon their shoulders and their spears upon the saddles of their horses, then march with them step by step’. The Messenger<sup>saww</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> said: ‘You are lying. But, the men of Yemen are better. The faith is in Yemen and the wisdom is in Yemen, and had it not been for the Emigration (Hijrat), I<sup>saww</sup> would have been of the people of Yemen.

The alienation and the cruelty is in the acreages[10] of the owners of the cotton yarn, Rabi’ah and Muzar from where the rays of the sun appear, and (as for) Muzhaj most of the tribe will enter the Paradise, and Hazramaut is better than Aamir Bin Sa’sa (and some have reported ‘better than Haaris Bin Muawiya’) and Bajeela is better than Ra’al and Zakwaan, and if Lihyaan were to perish Iasws would not care’.

Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Cursed four kings – Jamada, and Makhwasa, and Mashraha, and Abza’a, as well as Akhtam Al-Ammaradat. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Cursed Al-Muhallal (One who legalises a woman for her previous husband after three divorces from him) and the one to whom she has been made legal for, and the slave who does not obey his master, and the one who makes a claim for lineage, and the man who is effeminate (has feminine traits) and the woman who has masculine traits, and the one who innovates something new in Al-Islam or helps an innovator, and the one who kills someone other than the one who wants to kill him, or strike against someone other than the one who wants to strike him, and the one who curses his father’.

So a man said, ‘O Messenger<sup>saww</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, is there a man who curses his own father?’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Yes, he who curses the fathers and the mothers of the men, so he has cursed his own father. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Cursed Ra’la, and Zakwaan, and Azla, and Lahyaan, and the criminals of Asad, and Ghatfaan, and Abu Sufyan Bin Harb, and Shahbala of two teeth, and the two sons of Malikat Bin Jazeem, and Marwaan, and Howzat and Hownat’.
